questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed 200 times. About how many heads would you expect?
Explain the difference between experimental and theoretical probability, using rolling a die as an example.
questions.modelAnswer: Theoretical probability is worked out by reasoning: a fair die has 6 equally likely outcomes, so P(6) = 1/6. Experimental probability comes from actually rolling: if you roll 60 times and get 12 sixes, the experimental probability is 12/60 = 1/5. With more and more rolls, the experimental probability usually gets closer to the theoretical 1/6.
rubric: Mentions getting closer with more trials
